name: AD826
type: Bipolar high-speed low-power dual video op-amp
tagline: ADI's 50 MHz, 350 V/µs video dual; CD-player tweakers found it cleaner than the AD827, 'almost as good' as an OPA637.

lineage.note: Sole source. SPICE model 'Rev. A, 11/92', ©1993. Presumably the dual of the AD817 (inferred from matching specs).

part_numbers.note: Leaded PDIP-8, A grade, −40 to +85 °C. Reportedly in PDN 10_0081 Rev. B.
Lead-free PDIP (N-8), Digi-Key AD826ANZ-ND. Possibly discontinued per PDN 10_0081 (unconfirmed).
Leaded SOIC-8, A grade; probably replaced by AD826ARZ; still at brokers.
Lead-free SOIC-8 (R-8); REEL7 = 7-inch reel (LCSC C114171, Newark 60AK7396). Likely active.

key_specs.value: 1.5 pA/√Hz typ (table shows 1500, read as fA)
±2.5 V to ±18 V; +5 V to +36 V single
15 mA max both amps (7.5 mA max each); 6.8 mA/amp
90 mA short circuit; AOL spec'd at 50 mA into 150 Ω
0.5 mV typ, 2 mV max (3 mV over temp)
3.3 µA typ, 6.6 µA max (10 µA at Tmin)
NPN bipolar pair; unlimited capacitive-load drive
key_specs.source: ADI SPICE model Rev. A 11/92; AAE-25

reputation.summary: A niche CD-player rolling part, not a mainstream legend; ADI designed it for video, CATV, copiers, scanners and fax. A few Audio Asylum and diyAudio users heard it as cleaner, more open and more detailed than the AD827, one 'almost as good' as an OPA637. No independent measurements exist.
typical_uses: Buffers driving cables or capacitive loads
caveats: Thin evidence: a few forum posts, no published measurements. Soomal/DiyEden listed it for testing in 2005; no review followed.
High bias current (3.3 µA typ) causes DC offset with large resistances; noise 15 nV/√Hz.
Draws up to 15 mA per package; runs warmer than audio duals.
DIP versions reportedly discontinued; rollers need old stock or SOIC adapters.
50 MHz part: decouple tightly. Tangent's notes call ultra-fast op-amps a poor fit for simple headphone amps.

counterfeit_notes: No AD826 counterfeit reports. DIP versions are discontinued (reportedly PDN 10_0081 Rev. B), so 'new' DIP stock is old or suspect. Buy from Mouser, Digi-Key or Newark, not loose SOP-8 marketplace lots; check ADI logo, date code, Z suffix.

Read PDN 10_0081 Rev. B: does it cover AD826AN/ANZ only, or the whole family despite AD826ARZ-REEL7 stock?
Confirm the AAE-25 column headings (current noise, Ro) against the original article.
Capture THD, differential gain/phase and 0.1 dB flatness figures.
Do the AD826 and AD817 share a die? No PCN or die change is known.
